title: Better Quantum Computing Stock: IBM or D-Wave?
author: Rick Orford
description: IBM and D-Wave are competing in the quantum computing race, but the article suggests that financial strength, enterprise reach, and ability to sustain through a long development cycle may matter more than arriving first. IBM's established position and resources could prove decisive over D-Wave's specialized quantum approach.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: IBM is portrayed as having financial strength, enterprise reach, and the ability to withstand a long development cycle. The article suggests these factors could prove decisive in the quantum computing race, positioning IBM as the stronger long-term competitor despite not necessarily arriving first.

D-Wave is presented as a specialized quantum computing competitor racing toward commercial adoption, but the article implies it may lack the financial resources and staying power of IBM to sustain through the extended development cycle required for quantum computing commercialization.

title: 2 Tech Dividend Stocks That Offer High Yields and Payout Growth
author: Will Healy
description: The article highlights two mature tech companies offering attractive dividend yields above the S&P 500 average. IBM delivers a 2.9% yield with 31 consecutive years of dividend increases and strong free cash flow of $14.6 billion, supported by cloud transformation growth. HP offers a higher 4.1% yield with sustainable payouts, as its $3.8 billion free cash flow significantly exceeds its $1.1 billion dividend costs, though the stock has remained flat recently.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: IBM demonstrates strong fundamentals with 31 consecutive years of dividend increases, a sustainable 2.9% yield backed by $14.6 billion in free cash flow, successful cloud transformation under new leadership, and outperformance of the S&P 500 over five years at a reasonable 21 P/E ratio.

HP offers an attractive 4.1% dividend yield with multiple years of payout increases, strong dividend sustainability with $3.8 billion free cash flow versus $1.1 billion dividend costs, and a low 11 P/E ratio providing downside protection despite flat recent stock performance.
